title: Research Assistant Salary: Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay in Australia

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. faqs.q: Do research assistants get casual loading?

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Research Assistant Salary

If you are working as a research assistant in Australia, you might be paid by the hour or offered an annual salary. Knowing how to convert between the two helps you compare job offers and understand your take-home pay. This guide explains the conversion formula, the role of the national minimum wage, award rates, casual loading, superannuation, and tax. We use the keyword **research assistant salary** throughout to keep the focus on your situation.

### The Basic Conversion Formula

The standard way to estimate annual gross pay from an hourly rate is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks = annual gross salary**

For full-time work, we assume 38 ordinary hours per week, as defined by the Fair Work Commission. For example, if your research assistant salary is $35 per hour, your annual gross pay would be:

$35 × 38 × 52 = $69,160

If you work part-time, use your actual weekly hours. For casual roles, remember that the hourly rate often includes a 25% casual loading, but you should never type a rate that already includes loading into a calculator – instead, enter the base rate and add the loading separately.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The national minimum wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, or $1,004.90 per week. This is the legal floor for award/agreement-free employees. However, most research assistants are covered by a modern award, such as the *Higher Education Industry – Academic Staff – Award* or the *Research Award*. Award rates are typically higher than the national minimum wage and vary by classification, experience, and level of appointment.

To find the correct rate for your role, check the pay guides published by the Fair Work Ombudsman. These guides list minimum pay rates, allowances, and penalty rates for each award. The Fair Work Commission also provides a Modern Awards Pay Database with detailed classification data. For a research assistant salary, you would look at the classification that matches your duties and qualifications.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you are a casual research assistant, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base rate. This loading is paid instead of annual leave, sick leave, and public holiday pay. For example, if the base award rate is $30 per hour, the casual rate becomes $37.50 per hour. The loading is calculated on the base rate, not on a rate that already includes it.

Superannuation (super) is paid on top of your gross earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. So if your annual gross pay is $69,160, your employer must contribute an additional $8,299.20 to your super fund. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra cost for the employer.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Many research assistants are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply double your weekly pay. Using the example above:

- Weekly gross: $35 × 38 = $1,330
- Fortnightly gross: $1,330 × 2 = $2,660

This is before tax and any other deductions. Your take-home pay will be lower after tax and the Medicare levy.

### Tax on Your Research Assistant Salary

For the 2026–27 financial year, the Australian Tax Office (ATO) resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and above: $51,367 plus 45% of excess over $190,000

Additionally, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. For a research assistant earning $69,160, the estimated tax would be:

- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201 to $45,000: ($45,000 – $18,200) × 0.15 = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001 to $69,160: ($69,160 – $45,000) × 0.30 = $7,248
- Total tax: $4,020 + $7,248 = $11,268
- Medicare levy: $69,160 × 0.02 = $1,383.20
- Total deductions: $12,651.20
- Estimated take-home pay: $69,160 – $12,651.20 = $56,508.80 per year

This is an estimate only. It does not include the Medicare levy surcharge, HELP repayments, or salary packaging.

### Using the Timesheet and Other Tools

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It then calculates your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, plus estimated tax and super. For more detailed award information, visit our [pay guides](/blog) page. You can also check the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for the latest national rates.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Summary

Whether you are negotiating a research assistant salary or checking your current pay, the conversion formula is straightforward. Remember to use the correct award rate, account for casual loading if applicable, and understand that super is paid on top. Use the tools on this site to get a quick estimate, and always refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman or your enterprise agreement for precise figures.
